cases.sourceReview: Correct Group B ordinary-table count2 for200 on one floor, bounded toPC403.1/403.1.1; revised draft delivered instead of erasing the count.
cases.answerText: **The ordinary plumbing-table count is 2 drinking fountains.** The Group B business row requires 1 per 100 persons; applying that rate to the supplied 200-person load on one floor gives 2 (PC Table 403.1; PC § 403.1.1).

cases.label: correct
cases.sourceReview: Correctly prohibits substituting bottled-water dispensers underPC410.3.
cases.answerText: No. Bottled-water dispensers cannot substitute for any required drinking fountains; the code expressly prohibits that substitution (PC § 410.3). This applies to both of the required fountains.

cases.label: correct
cases.sourceReview: Correctly rejects a valve between boiler and relief valve;MC1006.5 supplied text expressly prohibits valves on either side.
cases.answerText: **No.** The 2022 NYC Mechanical Code requires the safety or relief valve to be installed directly in the boiler’s safety/relief-valve opening and prohibits valves on either side of that connection. A service shutoff between the boiler and relief valve is therefore not permitted. The relief-valve drain must also discharge by gravity to a nonhazardous point without obstruction (MC § 1006.5).

cases.label: correct
cases.sourceReview: Correctly keeps the discharge pipe at least equal to outletdiameter underMC1006.6, irrespective of proposed flow calculation.
cases.answerText: No. Under the 2022 NYC Mechanical Code, the discharge pipe must be at least the same diameter as the relief-valve outlet; a calculation showing adequate flow does not override that minimum (MC § 1006.6).

cases.label: correct
cases.sourceReview: Correct prohibition on manual dampers in appliance ventconnectors underFGC503.13; fixedbaffle distinction preserved.
cases.answerText: No. Under the 2022 NYC Fuel Gas Code, a manually operated damper may not be placed in any appliance’s vent connector. The text separately clarifies that fixed baffles are not classified as manually operated dampers; that clarification does not permit an adjustable manual damper. (FGC § 503.13)

cases.label: correct
cases.sourceReview: Correctly explains fixedbaffles are not manually operateddampers without asserting complete installation compliance.
cases.answerText: **No—not under the manually operated damper prohibition.** FGC § 503.13 expressly says fixed baffles “shall not be classified as manually operated dampers,” so that prohibition does not apply to a fixed baffle.

cases.sourceReview: Correct95percent950gallon limit and automaticshutoff requirement; complete scope andoperative5704.2.9.4 in boundFC5704text.
cases.answerText: **No.** For your stated 1,000-gallon aboveground tank storing combustible liquid, 950 gallons is the maximum fill level, but the Fire Code still requires an approved overfill-prevention system for the tank. During filling, that system must automatically stop liquid flow at 95% capacity; an operator alone cannot replace it (FC § 5704.2.9.4).
